stem: During a quarterly audit, reviewers find that some production fixes bypass the deployment pipeline and are applied straight to live instances. Which TWO practices close this gap? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Deploy changes as immutable images that replace the running instance rather than patching it in place.
Provision every resource from an infrastructure-as-code template instead of making console changes.
Apply patches directly to the currently running fleet on a fixed schedule.
Rely on Auto Scaling health checks to replace any instance that fails a check.
Schedule AWS Backup's policy-based backups for the fleet's volumes.

rationale: Replacing an instance with a new immutable image instead of patching it removes the path by which a running resource is changed outside the pipeline. Provisioning every resource from an infrastructure-as-code template, instead of editing resources through the console, keeps the template as the single source of truth for what is deployed. Scheduled in-place patching of the running fleet is itself the kind of direct, off-pipeline change the audit is flagging, so it does not close the gap. Auto Scaling health checks replace instances that fail a check, but they say nothing about how a deliberate application change reaches the fleet in the first place. Scheduling policy-based backups protects data for restoration, but it does not change how application or configuration changes are deployed to running instances.
